facts.detail: Under One Touch Switch the customer contacts the new broadband provider, which arranges the switch.
The customer supplies the address, current provider and services; matched records trigger switching information from the old provider.
The new provider arranges the preferred switching date where technically possible.
The old service ends automatically after the new service is confirmed working.

guard_streams.write_limit: Switching workflow does not prove parcel coverage, orderability or measured speed.

facts.detail: The old provider must not charge a notice period extending beyond the switching date.
Loss of service during a provider switch must not last longer than one working day.
Providers must compensate where the new service is delayed or the customer is left without service for more than one working day.
Missed service or installation appointments can also trigger compensation.

guard_streams.write_limit: Switch protections are customer-remedy evidence, not parcel network evidence.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom One Touch Switch one-year update

facts.detail: Ofcom published the one-year One Touch Switch update on 12 September 2025.
More than 1.6 million landline or broadband customers had used One Touch Switch in its first year.
More than 300 providers were signed up to the process.
The process applies across different fixed networks, including Openreach, cable and alternative fibre networks.

guard_streams.write_limit: Adoption totals and provider participation cannot establish exact parcel availability.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom new phone or broadband contract checklist

facts.detail: Providers must offer a contract option no longer than 12 months for each service they provide.
Residential and small-business service contracts should not exceed 24 months, subject to separate handset treatment.
Early termination charges should not exceed the payments remaining on the contract and may be lower.
A price increase beyond the agreed terms requires at least one month notice and a penalty-free exit right.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract length and exit rights do not indicate parcel serviceability.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom new phone or broadband contract checklist

facts.detail: Before consent, providers must supply a written one-page contract summary, or three pages for bundled services.
Detailed written contract information must also be supplied before the customer is bound.
Fixed-broadband sales information should explain minimum, normally available, maximum and advertised download and upload speeds.
Mobile-broadband information should explain estimated maximum and advertised download and upload speeds.

guard_streams.write_limit: Pre-sale speed disclosures are estimates and contractual information, not accepted parcel measurements.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom provider goes out of business guide

facts.detail: Where another company takes over a failed provider, service should usually continue without interruption.
The existing contract should normally transfer to the acquiring provider.
If the acquiring provider changes contract terms, the customer should have a penalty-free exit right.
Customers unhappy with the acquiring provider can switch, subject to checking contract status.

guard_streams.write_limit: Takeover continuity guidance cannot confirm current service at an individual parcel.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom provider goes out of business guide

facts.detail: Without a takeover, the failed provider should tell customers when service will stop.
Customers need to sign up with another provider to continue service.
Customers should not have to pay early termination charges in this scenario.
Keeping the existing telephone number may not be possible.

guard_streams.write_limit: Provider-failure outcomes do not establish alternative-network parcel availability.

facts.detail: The original Hampshire contract targeted around 75,500 premises for £104.2 million.
The original contract was signed in June 2023.
The May 2026 redesign revised the contract to around 29,000 premises backed by £71.7 million.
BDUK cited commercial rollout expansion and changed market conditions.

guard_streams.write_limit: Redesigned procurement totals are not exact parcel delivery evidence.

facts.detail: The original Suffolk contract targeted around 79,500 premises for £100.5 million.
The original contract was signed in June 2023.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 60,000 premises with up to £118.2 million investment.
Detailed planning and construction precede service, and premises can change for planning or technical reasons.

guard_streams.write_limit: Award and redesign scope cannot be promoted to current parcel orderability.

facts.detail: The original Norfolk contract targeted around 62,200 premises for £114.2 million.
The original contract was signed in June 2023.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 33,000 premises backed by £61.9 million.
The redesign is intended to reduce overlap and focus subsidy on premises otherwise missed.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional redesign intent cannot prove service at a specific address.

guard_streams.source: BDUK East and West Sussex contract redesign

facts.detail: The original East and West Sussex contract targeted around 52,000 premises for £100 million.
The original contract was signed in January 2024.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 13,000 premises backed by £25.2 million.
BDUK is discussing options for premises not covered by rollout plans.

guard_streams.write_limit: Redesign and supplier discussions cannot establish parcel-level completion.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Leicestershire and Warwickshire contract redesign

facts.detail: The original Leicestershire and Warwickshire contract targeted around 38,000 premises for £71 million.
The original contract was signed in January 2024.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 36,000 premises with up to £76.4 million investment.
Detailed planning and physical network construction are required before service access.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract scope and planned build cannot identify live parcels.

guard_streams.source: BDUK North Shropshire descope and reassignment

facts.detail: Freedom Fibre was awarded a North Shropshire contract covering 12,000 premises.
The update recorded 2,500 premises completed and a further 1,000 targeted by the end of June 2025.
BDUK and Freedom Fibre agreed to descope the remaining 8,500 premises.
In April 2026 premises in the area were added to Openreach call-off three.

guard_streams.write_limit: Descope and reassignment records cannot identify which parcels are currently served.

facts.detail: The May management table is a snapshot of data held on 21 May 2026.
Supplier resubmissions reduced previously reported built counts for Bedfordshire and North Shropshire.
Contracted figures cover initial scope and may exclude deferred premises.
Figures are rounded, subject to ingestion lag and not directly comparable with official statistics.

guard_streams.write_limit: Management corrections and snapshots cannot establish exact parcel delivery.
